cat > ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatBitsCompiled.fss <<EOF
(* On the compiled path, the simpleDoubleArith helpers that Float's bit, neighbour, narrowing, inequality, MIN, MAX and directed-rounding bindings and fromRawBits name give their values at zeros, large values, the smallest subnormal, the infinities and NaN. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyFloatBitsCompiled
export Executable

dToString(a:RR64):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleToString")
dNeg(a:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleNeg")
dSub(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSub")
dMul(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMul")
dDiv(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleDiv")
dPow(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doublePow")
fToD(a:RR32):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.floatToDouble")

dIsNaN(a:RR64):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleIsNaN")
dIsInfinite(a:RR64):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleIsInfinite")
dRawBits(a:RR64):ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleRawBits")
dNextUp(a:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleNextUp")
dNextDown(a:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleNextDown")
dToFloat(a:RR64):RR32 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleToFloat")
dNE(a:RR64, b:RR64):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleNE")
dMin(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMin")
dMax(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMax")
dAddUpNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleAddUpNoNaN")
dSubUpNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSubUpNoNaN")
dMulUpNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMulUpNoNaN")
dDivUpNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleDivUpNoNaN")
dSqrtUp(a:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSqrtUp")
dAddDownNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleAddDownNoNaN")
dSubDownNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSubDownNoNaN")
dMulDownNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMulDownNoNaN")
dDivDownNoNaN(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleDivDownNoNaN")
dSqrtDown(a:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSqrtDown")
dAddUp(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleAddUp")
dSubUp(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSubUp")
dMulUp(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMulUp")
dDivUp(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleDivUp")
dAddDown(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleAddDown")
dSubDown(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleSubDown")
dMulDown(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleMulDown")
dDivDown(a:RR64, b:RR64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleDivDown")
dFromRawBits(a:ZZ64):RR64 = builtinPrimitive("$P.doubleFromRawBits")

run():() = do
  z: RR64 = 0.0
  nz: RR64 = dNeg(z)
  one: RR64 = 1.0
  two: RR64 = 2.0
  three: RR64 = 3.0
  a: RR64 = 2.5
  b: RR64 = dNeg(0.75)
  p1: RR64 = 0.1
  p2: RR64 = 0.2
  large: RR64 = 1000000000000000000000.0
  huge: RR64 = dMul(dMul(large, large), dMul(large, large))
  huge2: RR64 = dMul(huge, huge)
  inf: RR64 = dMul(dMul(huge, huge), dMul(huge, huge))
  ninf: RR64 = dNeg(inf)
  nan: RR64 = dDiv(z, z)
  tiny: RR64 = dPow(two, dNeg(1074.0))
  ntiny: RR64 = dNeg(tiny)
  minZZ64: ZZ64 = -9223372036854775807
  minZZ64 := minZZ64 - 1

  assert(dToString(tiny) = "4.9E-324", "the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dToString(huge2) = "1.0000000000000001E168", "1.0E84 times 1.0E84")

  assert(NOT dIsNaN(z), "dIsNaN of 0.0")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(nz), "dIsNaN of -0.0")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(one), "dIsNaN of 1.0")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(large), "dIsNaN of a large value")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(tiny), "dIsNaN of the smallest subnormal")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(inf), "dIsNaN of infinity")
  assert(NOT dIsNaN(ninf), "dIsNaN of -infinity")
  assert(dIsNaN(nan), "dIsNaN of 0.0 / 0.0")
  assert(dIsNaN(dSub(inf, inf)), "dIsNaN of infinity - infinity")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(z), "dIsInfinite of 0.0")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(nz), "dIsInfinite of -0.0")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(b), "dIsInfinite of -0.75")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(large), "dIsInfinite of a large value")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(tiny), "dIsInfinite of the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dIsInfinite(inf), "dIsInfinite of infinity")
  assert(dIsInfinite(ninf), "dIsInfinite of -infinity")
  assert(dIsInfinite(dMul(huge2, huge2)), "dIsInfinite of an overflow")
  assert(NOT dIsInfinite(nan), "dIsInfinite of NaN")

  assert(dRawBits(z) = 0, "dRawBits of 0.0")
  assert(dRawBits(nz) = minZZ64, "dRawBits of -0.0")
  assert(dRawBits(one) = 4607182418800017408, "dRawBits of 1.0")
  assert(dRawBits(a) = 4612811918334230528, "dRawBits of 2.5")
  assert(dRawBits(b) = -4618441417868443648, "dRawBits of -0.75")
  assert(dRawBits(p1) = 4591870180066957722, "dRawBits of 0.1")
  assert(dRawBits(large) = 4921056587992461136, "dRawBits of a large value")
  assert(dRawBits(tiny) = 1, "dRawBits of the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dRawBits(inf) = 9218868437227405312, "dRawBits of infinity")
  assert(dRawBits(ninf) = -4503599627370496, "dRawBits of -infinity")
  assert(dIsNaN(dFromRawBits(dRawBits(nan))), "dRawBits of NaN, read back")

  assert(dToString(dNextUp(z)) = "4.9E-324", "dNextUp of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(one)) = "1.0000000000000002", "dNextUp of 1.0")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(a)) = "2.5000000000000004", "dNextUp of 2.5")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(b)) = "-0.7499999999999999", "dNextUp of -0.75")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(large)) = "1.0000000000000001E21", "dNextUp of a large value")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(tiny)) = "9.9E-324", "dNextUp of the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(ntiny)) = "-0.0", "dNextUp of minus the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(inf)) = "Infinity", "dNextUp of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(ninf)) = "-1.7976931348623157E308", "dNextUp of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNextUp(nan)) = "NaN", "dNextUp of NaN")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(one)) = "0.9999999999999999", "dNextDown of 1.0")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(a)) = "2.4999999999999996", "dNextDown of 2.5")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(b)) = "-0.7500000000000001", "dNextDown of -0.75")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(large)) = "9.999999999999999E20", "dNextDown of a large value")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(tiny)) = "0.0", "dNextDown of the smallest subnormal")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(nz)) = "-4.9E-324", "dNextDown of -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(inf)) = "1.7976931348623157E308", "dNextDown of infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(ninf)) = "-Infinity", "dNextDown of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dNextDown(nan)) = "NaN", "dNextDown of NaN")

  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(a))) = "2.5", "dToFloat of 2.5")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(b))) = "-0.75", "dToFloat of -0.75")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(p1))) = "0.10000000149011612", "dToFloat of 0.1")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(z))) = "0.0", "dToFloat of 0.0")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(nz))) = "-0.0", "dToFloat of -0.0")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(large))) = "1.000000020040877E21", "dToFloat of a large value")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(huge))) = "Infinity", "dToFloat of 1.0E84 overflows")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(tiny))) = "0.0", "dToFloat of the smallest subnormal underflows")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(inf))) = "Infinity", "dToFloat of infinity")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(ninf))) = "-Infinity", "dToFloat of -infinity")
  assert(dToString(fToD(dToFloat(nan))) = "NaN", "dToFloat of NaN")

  assert(dNE(a, b), "dNE")
  assert(NOT dNE(a, a), "dNE of equal values")
  assert(NOT dNE(z, nz), "dNE of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(NOT dNE(inf, inf), "dNE of infinities")
  assert(dNE(inf, ninf), "dNE of infinity and -infinity")
  assert(dNE(large, inf), "dNE of a large value and infinity")
  assert(dNE(tiny, z), "dNE of the smallest subnormal and 0.0")
  assert(NOT dNE(tiny, tiny), "dNE of the smallest subnormal and itself")

  assert(dToString(dMin(a, b)) = "-0.75", "dMin")
  assert(dToString(dMin(b, a)) = "-0.75", "dMin, swapped")
  assert(dToString(dMin(z, nz)) = "-0.0", "dMin of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMin(nz, z)) = "-0.0", "dMin of -0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMin(large, inf)) = "1.0E21", "dMin of a large value and infinity")
  assert(dToString(dMin(ninf, b)) = "-Infinity", "dMin of -infinity and b")
  assert(dToString(dMin(tiny, z)) = "0.0", "dMin of the smallest subnormal and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMax(a, b)) = "2.5", "dMax")
  assert(dToString(dMax(b, a)) = "2.5", "dMax, swapped")
  assert(dToString(dMax(z, nz)) = "0.0", "dMax of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMax(nz, z)) = "0.0", "dMax of -0.0 and 0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMax(nz, nz)) = "-0.0", "dMax of -0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dMax(large, inf)) = "Infinity", "dMax of a large value and infinity")
  assert(dToString(dMax(ninf, b)) = "-0.75", "dMax of -infinity and b")
  assert(dToString(dMax(tiny, z)) = "4.9E-324", "dMax of the smallest subnormal and 0.0")

  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(p1, p2)) = "0.30000000000000004", "dAddUpNoNaN, inexact")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(one, two)) = "3.0", "dAddUpNoNaN, exact")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(large, one)) = "1.0000000000000001E21", "dAddUpNoNaN of a large value and 1")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(tiny, one)) = "1.0000000000000002", "dAddUpNoNaN of the smallest subnormal and 1")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(tiny, tiny)) = "9.9E-324", "dAddUpNoNaN of two smallest subnormals")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(z, nz)) = "0.0", "dAddUpNoNaN of 0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(nz, nz)) = "-0.0", "dAddUpNoNaN of -0.0 and -0.0")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(inf, one)) = "Infinity", "dAddUpNoNaN of infinity and 1")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(inf, ninf)) = "Infinity", "dAddUpNoNaN of infinity and -infinity")
  assert(dToString(dAddUpNoNaN(nan, one)) = "NaN", "dAddUpNoNaN of NaN and 1")

## B.12 Native code and Java interop

The two worlds bind native code by two mechanisms that share nothing but the word "native".

Interpreter: a function whose body is literally `builtinPrimitive("some.java.Class")` is pattern-matched in `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-229`). A string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` names a static Java method, `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method"`: `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` takes, among the class's public static methods of that name, the one whose Java types carry the declared types, `self` first, and calls it by reflection, each argument unboxed and the result boxed (`NativeApp.java:200-207`; since rung W, `640acb4a1`; F-299). Any other string names a class — a subclass of `NativeFn0..3`/`NativeMeth0..3` in `interpreter/glue/` — which is loaded reflectively and takes the evaluator's boxed `FValue`s directly.

There are 231 such bindings in `LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, 108 in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and 7 in `LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss`.

Compiler: a `.fss` writes `import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{class.method => name, …}` (16 such lines in `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, 3 in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`); `ForeignJava` reads the Java class with ASM to synthesize an api for it (`repository/ForeignJava.java:132-136,565-575`), and `FortressTransformer` rewrites the class into a wrapper whose methods take and return the compiled world's boxed values (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressTransformer.java:37`, wrapper written to `nativewrapper_cache` at `:33`).

`import java` also works on the interpreter path, by a third route that is easy to miss: `ForeignComponentWrapper` populates an environment from `ForeignJava`'s synthesized declarations (`interpreter/env/ForeignComponentWrapper.java:59`), and `ClosureMaker` generates, at run time, a `NativeFn<n>` subclass that calls the Java method and writes it into `bytecode_cache` (`interpreter/env/ClosureMaker.java:44-50,52`).

No test under `ProjectFortress/tests/` uses `import java` (0 files), while 2 under `compiler_tests/` do, so the interpreter's foreign-Java route is present but not exercised by the gated suite.

There is no way for a Fortress program to be called *from* Java other than by loading the generated classes through `InstantiatingClassloader`, which is what `MainWrapper` does.

# Rung F: the floating-point family, Float's 30

- problem: Float's 30 bindings are among the 83 that fit a helper as a bare string and still named a glue class (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/families-base.tsv`, its 30 lines of family F; `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:397`), and walk's loader refused a declared `Float`: the planner's move of `Float`'s `+` alone stopped every program at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter b.' - historical: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss` (`StaticNativeApp.java` is the revival's, not in a874948ac)

## How the rung ran

The worktree was seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base23` by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 4 s) and the branch pushed. The tests came first: the carry test seen failing through the harness on the base's code at 11:48:45 UTC, before any edit; the two guards seen passing there (walk 11:49:18, compiled 11:53:00); then the patch applied, built at 12:00 ('BUILD SUCCESSFUL', 'Caches … started again, empty'), the library order (five jars), the tests on the edit, a one-binding mutant sweep of the guard, the old code beside the new, the suites, the stages and the ladder subset. ## What changed and why

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:51`, `javaFor`: `if (t.equals("RR64") || t.equals("Float")) return double.class;`. A `Float` is walk's run-time `RR64` (`FFloat`); `unbox` reads a Java `double` from any value by `getFloat()` (`:196`), and `box` makes an `FFloat` of a `double` whatever the declared name (`:218`), so the one line is the whole carry, for a parameter and for a result. Twelve of the 30 declare a parameter `Float`; without the line walk refuses the library at load.
- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:55-193`, `value object Float`, 30 strings, each the one line after its header, one line for one: `asString` and `asExprString` (`:56`, `:58`, `doubleToString`), `opr |self|` (`:80`, `doubleAbs`), `=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (`:82`, `:86`, `:88`, `:90`, `:92`; `doubleEQ`, `doubleLT`, `doubleLE`, `doubleGT`, `doubleGE`), the unary `-` (`:102`, `doubleNeg`), `+`, `-`, `DOT`, `TIMES`, juxtaposition, `/` (`:104`, `:106`, `:108`, `:110`, `:113`, `:115`; `doubleAdd`, `doubleSub`, `doubleMul` three times, `doubleDiv`), `SQRT` (`:117`, `doubleSQRT`), `^` at a `Float` and at an `RR64` exponent (`:155`, `:159`, `doublePow`), `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `log`, `exp` (`:165` to `:181`, `doubleSin` to `doubleExp`), `floor`, `ceiling` (`:183`, `:187`), `truncate`, `round` (`:191`, `:193`, `doubleTruncate`, `doubleRound`, at `ZZ64`, fork 11). content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then

            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1

        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"

}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"

98:- `record.md` carries, as complete findings, the FACTS entry the rung earns, its ledger notes, the whole new line of each row whose claim its change alters, its new rows, the handover line, and a "Revival change" section, or "Revival change: none" with the reason. The section is material for the skill writer, not skill text, in two labelled parts: "The change", as evidence (the team's source and what it says or does, with `file:line`; what the tree now does, with its test; the reason, as a passage, a checker refusal or a measured failure), and "Provenance" (the question or item, the answer or default it follows, the batch). The worker is told: "Name no question, item, batch, rung or record file in the change, and give no decision's status there; provenance goes in its own part." (the `coordinator` skill's `references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"; `reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "Proposed fix to the mechanism", item 2.)
99-- `REPORT.md` opens with five provenance lines: problem, spec, precedent, deviation, historical. The `historical:` line names every file of the 2012 tree the rung edits, for the commit message (the protocol's hard rule on the gate).
100-- The worker does not edit FACTS, the ledger, PLAN, POSITIONS, INDEX, the handover, the tools or `.claude/`: the gather folds `record.md` into them, since every rung would conflict there.
101-- It commits and pushes its own files on its branch as it goes, so a dead container loses nothing.
102-- A resume after a kill runs it again from its start with the same brief, which no retry's head reaches (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "Interrupts and process stops"). So step 1 of the brief says that the commits past the base, or in a resume or repair round those after the one that carries the judge's ruling, and the uncommitted edits are its earlier launch's; that the head it reached is the newest of those commits; and where that launch's transcript is, with any extract of it under the worktree's `tmp/`. In climb batch 23 both resumed workers found their predecessors' transcripts on their own and wrote their extracts in the session's scratchpad, and rung W ran its tests on the base's code again (`reviews/batch-23-review.md`, findings 2 and 4).
103-- It writes `REPORT.md`, `record.md` and a decision record through a Bash heredoc or a script, not the `Write` tool: in climb batch 24 the harness refused the `Write` of `REPORT.md` to four of the seven workers, 'Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files.', and none of the three that wrote it through a heredoc (`reviews/batch-24-review.md`, finding 5).
104-- Its result carries `reportText` and `recordText` word for word, since the harness often refuses a worker's write of those files; `decisions`, each with the ways not taken, which its skeptic weighs its fixes against; `pointsReached`; and `forCurator`, its questions for the curator.
--
163:- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there").
164-- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
165-- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
166-- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
167:- **After the rungs.** One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). """The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).
